Nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus are essential for the growth
and maintenance of plant and animal life. However, high nutrient
concentrations in the water column may fuel the growth of harmful algae,
creating dense blooms that block sunlight and deplete oxygen for fish
and other organisms. Nutrients enter water bodies several ways including
runoff from rain events, and atmospheric deposition from natural and
industrial sources. Analysis of the changes in nitrogen and phosphorus
concentrations aids the management of nutrient pollution and helps
reduce the frequency and severity of harmful algal blooms.
